name: Tool From Mesh
description: Construct a ToolModel from a Rhino mesh and a TCP plane, both expressed in the coordinates the mesh was modelled in. Wire `base_plane` to say where the robot's flange takes hold of the geometry, so the tool can be modelled wherever is convenient. The same mesh is used for collision checking unless a separate `collision_mesh` is provided. Output feeds directly into a Load Robot Cell component's `tools` input.

inputParameters.name: name
inputParameters.description: Tool identifier (used as the tool id when added to a cell). Defaults to `attached_tool`.

inputParameters.name: visual_mesh
inputParameters.description: Rhino mesh for visualization (and collision checking if no separate collision mesh is provided).

inputParameters.name: collision_mesh
inputParameters.description: Optional Rhino mesh used only for collision checking. Defaults to `visual_mesh`.

inputParameters.name: tcp_plane
inputParameters.description: Tool Coordinate Frame, as a Rhino Plane or COMPAS Frame, expressed in the coordinates the mesh was modelled in.

inputParameters.name: base_plane
inputParameters.description: Optional plane, in the coordinates the mesh was modelled in, at which the robot's flange takes hold of the tool. Its Z axis points away from the robot: a tool drawn reaching along world Z needs none. For a tool drawn reaching along world X, wire the plane with Z = world X. Defaults to the world XY plane, i.e. the modelling coordinates are the tool's base frame.
